assets.planningDesc: Maps, force graphs, timelines, and system trees all extend from the world handbook. Organize the rules, forces, locations, and tensions first, then generate visual assets.
assets.preset.forceDesc: Organize forces, factions, allies, rivals, and vassal relations into a visual relationship network.
assets.preset.forceReadiness: First add the major forces, current objectives, and mutual pressure.
assets.preset.mapDesc: Use regions, roads, borders, and story locations to explain how characters move and where conflict erupts.
assets.preset.mapReadiness: First add the story stage, location risks, and force-controlled areas.
assets.preset.powerDesc: Organize power sources, progression paths, costs, and taboo boundaries into a hierarchy.
assets.preset.powerReadiness: First add the core rules, costs, and boundaries that can't be broken.
assets.preset.relationDesc: Connect characters to forces, locations, resources, and taboos to reduce setting drift.
assets.preset.relationReadiness: First add character affiliations, faction pressure, and key locations.
assets.preset.timelineDesc: Record major events, catastrophes, dynastic changes, and situational shifts so the world's progress has a trajectory.
assets.preset.timelineReadiness: First add the core conflict, shared consequences, and key historical nodes.
assets.publishDescPlaceholder: Optional description (defaults to the current layer content if left blank)
assets.saveCurrentAsAsset: Save current settings as a world asset
assets.tool.importDesc: Create a world from text, Markdown, or JSON.
assets.tool.libraryDesc: Reuse content you can accumulate, such as locations, forces, and resources.
assets.tool.referencesDesc: Link materials that support the world settings.
assets.tool.snapshotsDesc: Save versions and compare differences between two settings.
axioms.desc: Think of these as "the underlying rules this world can't casually break." Later auto-generation and handbook checks reference them.
axioms.title: Core rules (axioms)
consistency.desc: Check whether core rules, genre signals, the power system, and conflict support contradict each other. Handle any issues one by one.
consistency.detailFallback: Cross-check this risk against the world handbook.
consistency.emptyReport: After running a check, the handbook checkup results and issues to handle appear here.
consistency.noIssues: No consistency issues recorded yet; results appear here after you run a check.
consistency.title: World handbook checkup
deepening.answerNote: This answer will be used to complete the world handbook.
deepening.desc: The system asks a few questions based on this world handbook. Your answers are merged into the world settings to clarify rules, forces, locations, and conflicts.
deepening.emptyState: Questions that help shape the world appear here. After generating them, fill in each one.
deepening.noQuickOptions: You can write your own answer directly, or describe the direction in one sentence first.
deepening.quickOptionsLabel: Answer directions you can use directly
deepening.subtitle: Fill the key gaps in the world handbook
deepening.title: Complete the world handbook
factions.baseOfPowerPlaceholder: Power base / resource source / control leverage
factions.factionCardNote: A faction card describes an abstract alignment, not a concrete company, department, or personal network.
factions.factionNamePlaceholder: Faction name, e.g. establishment stability wing / market profit wing / network pragmatist wing
factions.forceCardNote: A force card describes a concrete organization or circle that can apply pressure, hold locations, and take part in relationship networks.
factions.forceNamePlaceholder: Force name, e.g. ad agency management / real-estate brokerage chain / local business network
factions.forceSummaryPlaceholder: Force overview / public identity / role in the world
factions.forceTypePlaceholder: Force type, e.g. company / department / brokerage network / business circle
factions.legend1: Faction = an abstract stance, line, or side in the world; Force = a concrete organization, circle, network, or institution.
factions.legend2: World-level default rules like "social pressure mechanisms," "industry operating rules," or "interpersonal network laws" should go into the "Rules Center" first, not be stuffed into faction cards.
factions.narrativeRolePlaceholder: Narrative role, e.g. oppressor / tempter / gatekeeper / buffer
factions.objectivePlaceholder: Current objective / what it wants to push now
factions.pressurePlaceholder: How it pressures / source of pressure / how it forces characters
factions.repForcesPlaceholder: Representative force IDs, separated by commas
handbook.aiAssistDesc: Let AI complete a handbook block from existing content; you can keep editing before saving.
handbook.card.forcesDesc: {{count}} forces determine character affiliation, faction pressure, and resource competition.
handbook.card.locationsDesc: {{count}} locations carry openings, power-ups, turning points, showdowns, and map assets.
handbook.card.rulesDesc: {{count}} rules constrain power, resources, taboos, and costs.
handbook.card.tensionDesc: Record force relations, location control, shared consequences, and taboo combinations to keep the world writable.
handbook.editingBanner: Organizing the selected block; saving updates the handbook overview above.
handbook.entryRiskJoinFallback: Add the resistance, cost, or identity risk of entering locations.
handbook.field.conflictHint: This isn't background info but the problem that character actions, faction conflicts, and chapter events revolve around repeatedly.
handbook.field.conflictPlaceholder: e.g. the dying star-core makes cultivators fight over lifespan, the court wants to bury the truth, and border demons invade in the chaos.
handbook.field.conflictTitle: The contradiction that can keep driving the plot
handbook.field.impressionHint: Let the author and AI instantly know this world's type, era feel, and central wonder.
handbook.field.impressionPlaceholder: e.g. a xianxia dynasty whose star-core is running dry
handbook.field.summaryHint: Write a short paragraph the author can restate directly; no need to split it into geography, culture, or history fields.
handbook.field.summaryPlaceholder: Use a paragraph to tell the author what this world looks like and where the story begins.
handbook.field.summaryTitle: The world's first glance for readers
handbook.field.themesHint: Separate with commas to help later characters, locations, and conflicts keep the same genre direction.
handbook.field.toneHint: Decides whether the story is dark, hot-blooded, light comedic, scheming, or adventurous exploration.
handbook.field.tonePlaceholder: Dark epic, light comedic adventure, power struggles...
handbook.forceRelationsJoinFallback: Add who allies, opposes, competes with, or exploits whom.
handbook.forcesJoinFallback: Once you add the major forces, character identities and faction conflicts become clearer.
handbook.headerDesc: First get a clear read on this world's impression, core rules, major forces, story stage, and conflict tension; enter the relevant block when you need fine-tuning.
handbook.letAiOrganize: Let AI organize the world handbook
handbook.locationsJoinFallback: Add opening, trial, conflict, or revelation locations.
handbook.pressureJoinFallback: Add the pressure forces put on the protagonist and world order.
handbook.previewConflictFallback: Add a problem that repeatedly creates character choices, faction conflicts, and chapter events.
handbook.previewConflictLabel: The contradiction that keeps driving the plot
handbook.previewFirstLookFallback: Add this world's first-glance imagery, order, danger, or wonder.
handbook.previewImpressionFallback: Add a one-line world impression so the author instantly grasps the genre, era feel, and central wonder.
handbook.previewRuleSummaryFallback: Add the hard rules of how the world works to keep character abilities and plot resolutions from going out of control.
handbook.previewToneFallback: Add the reading vibe, e.g. hot-blooded leveling, dark epic, light comedic adventure, or power struggles.
handbook.rulesJoinFallback: Add 2-3 core rules that must be followed.
handbook.sharedConsequencesJoinFallback: Add the world-wide consequences of breaking rules or escalating conflict.
handbook.title: Organize the world handbook
handbookForce.description: First help the author see who competes for resources, who creates obstacles, and where characters might come from. {{summary}}
handbookForce.nameHint: Organizations a character might come from, join, betray, or oppose.
handbookForce.namePlaceholder: Star-Emperor Court, Tianji Pavilion, Demon Alliance
handbookForce.objectiveHint: Objectives turn into chapter events and character conflicts.
handbookForce.objectivePlaceholder: Fight over mines, bury the truth, find the lost heir
handbookForce.pressureHint: It forces the protagonist or other forces to choose, flee, bargain, or go to war.
handbookForce.pressurePlaceholder: Hunt the protagonist, control resources, start wars, trigger a trust crisis
handbookForce.pressureTitle: Pressure it brings to the story
handbookForce.summaryFallback: Once you add the major forces, character identities, faction conflicts, and chapter pressure become steadier.
handbookForce.summaryHint: Spell out its stance, resources, and the traits readers should remember.
handbookForce.summaryPlaceholder: What does this force represent in the world?
handbookForce.summaryTitle: What it represents in the world
handbookForce.title: Major forces
handbookForce.typeHint: Helps AI judge how it acts and the feel of the organization.
handbookLocation.description: Turn the world into concrete locations: where the story opens, where power-ups fit, and where conflict erupts.
handbookLocation.nameHint: Later maps, force-controlled areas, and chapter venues revolve around these locations.
handbookLocation.namePlaceholder: Northern Ice Plains, Star Ruins City, Black Tide Port
handbookLocation.narrativeHint: Helps chapter planning decide whether it suits an opening, trial, turning point, or showdown.
handbookLocation.narrativePlaceholder: Opening, trial, turning point, showdown, revelation
handbookLocation.riskHint: Risks become resistance to character actions and chapter conflicts.
handbookLocation.riskPlaceholder: Being hunted, resources depleted, identity exposed, rules failing
handbookLocation.summaryHint: Spell out this location's imagery, order, danger, or wonder.
handbookLocation.summaryPlaceholder: What's the reader's first impression of this location?
handbookLocation.terrainHint: Give the location a memorable sense of space rather than being just a name.
handbookLocation.terrainPlaceholder: Snowfield frontier, floating city, underground mines, sea fortress
handbookLocation.title: Story stage
handbookRule.boundaryHint: Prevents later plots from breaking world credibility just to solve problems.
handbookRule.boundaryPlaceholder: No one revives without cost; low-tier characters can't bypass sealing rules.
handbookRule.boundaryTitle: Boundaries that can't be casually broken
handbookRule.costHint: The cost that must be paid when using, breaking, or circumventing the rule.
handbookRule.costPlaceholder: Lifespan, memory, identity, resources, faction trust...
handbookRule.description: These rules constrain character identity, power boundaries, and conflict sources, the underlying settings most important to follow while writing this book.
handbookRule.meaningHint: Spell out how characters, forces, and chapter events are affected by this rule.
handbookRule.meaningPlaceholder: What does this rule mean in the story?
handbookRule.nameHint: A short phrase is enough so the author can reference it repeatedly while writing.
handbookRule.namePlaceholder: Star-core borrowing, bloodline is irreversible, no casting in the Forbidden City
handbookRule.summaryHint: Use a paragraph to explain how power, resources, taboos, and consequences together constrain this world.
handbookRule.summaryPlaceholder: e.g. all extraordinary power is borrowed from the star-core; using it beyond your tier drains lifespan and is logged by Tianji Pavilion.
handbookRule.title: Core rules
handbookTension.advancedNote: Enter advanced field maintenance when you need to fine-tune force relations, location control, or import structured data. Regular authors only need to maintain this page's handbook content.
handbookTension.conflictHint: Long-term contradictions among resources, order, power systems, or faction goals.
handbookTension.conflictPlaceholder: e.g. resource depletion, collapsing order, two power systems that reject each other.
handbookTension.consequencesHint: One per line; write the long-term costs the world's rules bring.
handbookTension.consequencesPlaceholder:
The stronger the power, the closer to corruption
The more prosperous the city, the more it relies on dangerous resources
handbookTension.description: Compress world settings into problems that keep driving the plot, so the world isn't just background material.
handbookTension.tabooHint: One per line; state which character backgrounds, power uses, or plot solutions must not appear.
handbookTension.tabooPlaceholder:
Mortals can't control the star-core without cost
Court spies can't openly join the demon faction
handbookTension.title: Key tensions
layersTab.generateAllHintInitial: The system organizes the world handbook into six writing summaries: foundation, power, society, culture, history, and conflict.
layersTab.generateAllHintRedo: With a world skeleton, summaries are organized from the handbook; only older worlds without a skeleton fill in missing layers.
layersTab.generateSixFirst: First AI generation of six layers
layersTab.title: Organize the world by layer
libraryPick.desc: The old V2 let you pick assets from the attribute library before formal generation. This keeps that idea but wires it into the current blueprint structure.
libraryPick.searchPlaceholder: Search asset library entries; filter by name or keyword
libraryPick.title: Preload from the asset library
overview.assetEntryDesc: Maps and graphs are visual assets of the world handbook; they don't take part in auto-sync overwrite and don't replace the handbook's rule source.
overview.assetForceDesc: Holds force nodes, allies and rivals, control relations, and power comparisons.
overview.assetMapDesc: Holds regions, location connectivity, story venues, and conflict heat.
overview.assetPowerDesc: Holds tiers, resources, costs, taboos, and breakthrough boundaries.
overview.assetTimelineDesc: Holds historical events, situational shifts, and world progress as the novel advances.
overview.coreConflictFallback: Once you add the core conflict, the system can more easily turn the world into ongoing plot pressure.
overview.coreRulesFallback: Enter handbook editing to add the rules this world must follow.
overview.emptyBlockForcesDesc: Organize the organizations, factions, interest groups, and pressure sources that drive the plot.
overview.emptyBlockRulesDesc: Record the underlying rules, costs, and taboo combinations this world can't casually break.
overview.emptyBlockStageDesc: Mark the key locations for openings, power-ups, conflict outbreaks, and turning points.
overview.emptyBlockTensionDesc: Capture the resource contradictions, faction conflicts, and rule costs that repeatedly create conflict.
overview.emptyDesc: The world handbook organizes scattered settings into rules, forces, locations, and plot pressure, making it easy for the author to understand and for the book to use.
overview.emptySummaryFallback: First have AI or handbook editing organize the world skeleton, then use it as a reusable world sample.
overview.majorForcesFallback: Enter handbook editing to add the forces and factions that drive the plot.
overview.priorityTitle: Prioritize these when using this world in your book
overview.provide1: Character identity boundaries, force affiliations, and taboo combinations.
overview.provide2: Opening locations, progression paths, and conflict sources.
overview.provide3: Rules that must be followed consistently while writing.
overview.provideTitle: As a world sample it can provide
overview.rulesSummaryFallback: Core rules constrain character identity, conflict sources, and world consistency.
overview.storyLocationsFallback: Enter handbook editing to add story locations suited to openings, power-ups, and turning points.
overview.summaryFallback: Add a one-line world overview that creators can grasp quickly.
overview.tabooFallback: No taboo combinations recorded. Add them in handbook editing when you need strong constraints.
overview.tensionsFallback: Enter handbook editing to add world contradictions that keep generating plot pressure.
overview.title: World handbook
overview.worldPromiseFallback: Once the world handbook is complete, this becomes a world sample your novel can reuse.
propertyOption.detailPlaceholder: Optional: add your preferences, such as what to keep, amplify, or limit.
propertyOption.empty: No usable key directions yet. This usually means the previous analysis failed; go back to step 1 and regenerate.
refMode.adaptWorld.desc: Keep the source world's base, then decide which rules, forces, and location structures can be reworked.
refMode.adaptWorld.label: Adapt the source into an original world
refMode.extractBase.desc: First extract a stable skeleton of the source world, then expand mostly around the source's facts.
refMode.extractBase.label: Extract the source world's foundation
refMode.toneRebuild.desc: Keep the atmosphere, relationship structure, and everyday feel, but allow substantial rebuilding of world facts.
refMode.toneRebuild.label: Rebuild using only the source's tone and structure
refSeed.empty: This time no directly reusable organizations, locations, or rules were reliably extracted from the reference work; generation will continue following your adaptation direction.
refSeed.factions.desc: Who sides with whom, what they believe, and what they push for. Good for keeping the source's big directions.
refSeed.factions.title: Faction stances
refSeed.forces.desc: Concrete organizations, such as companies, departments, gangs, and personal networks, that can appear directly.
refSeed.forces.title: Organizations and forces
refSeed.headerDesc: The system extracts a batch of reusable settings from the reference work and checks them by default. Keeping them significantly reduces later manual entry.
refSeed.locations.desc: Scenes you can use directly, such as cities, neighborhoods, companies, and residences.
refSeed.locations.title: Locations and scenes
refSeed.recognized: Recognized as a directly reusable source setting.
refSeed.rules.desc: How this world runs by default; later auto-generation references these underlying rules.
refSeed.rules.title: Source rules
relations.novelSuggestDesc: A read-only view of the directions available once the world sample enters a novel.
stepOne.allowedPlaceholder: e.g. city tiers, social rules, power networks, location systems
stepOne.extracted: Auto-segmented extraction: {{length}} source characters, split into {{count}} segments.
stepOne.forbiddenPlaceholder: e.g. no supernatural elements, no power-fantasy leveling, no drifting from real-world social logic
stepOne.genreEmpty: The genre base library is empty. Creating a world sample requires available genre bases first.
stepOne.genreFooter: Settle on the genre base first, then generate the concept card, world attributes, and later skeleton choices.
stepOne.genreHint: The genre base determines reader expectations, power rules, and common conflicts for the world.
stepOne.inspiration.free.desc: Best when you already have ideas about the genre, tone, or story stage.
stepOne.inspiration.free.title: Start from one line of inspiration
stepOne.inspiration.random.desc: Best when you have no clear idea yet and just want a usable world starting point.
stepOne.inspiration.random.title: Let AI suggest a direction
stepOne.inspiration.reference.desc: Best for borrowing the feel of an existing work and then generating an independent original world.
stepOne.inspiration.reference.title: Adapt from a reference work
stepOne.inspirationPlaceholder.free: Describe the world's tone, stage, conflicts, or power source in a few sentences
stepOne.inspirationPlaceholder.random: Optional: note genres you want to avoid, the mood you like, or your target readers
stepOne.inspirationPlaceholder.reference: Paste source excerpts, a world summary, or your understanding of the work; you can also use only the knowledge base documents above
stepOne.knowledgeDesc: What you pick here is the reference source; the system first extracts the source world's anchors, then generates adaptation directions.
stepOne.preferencesHint: By default it produces 6 standard world attributes; you usually don't need to change this.
stepOne.preservePlaceholder: e.g. a real-world urban base, the feel of renting, the emotional tug of adult life
stepOne.progressSteps.free: This step runs in order: organize the inspiration input, generate the concept card, and generate the preliminary attribute options.
stepOne.progressSteps.reference: This step runs in order: organize reference material, extract the source world's anchors, and generate adaptation decisions.
stepOne.worldNameHint: You can leave the name blank; the system first creates a world sample you can keep refining.
stepOne.worldNamePlaceholder: e.g. Zixia Realm, Ashen Dynasty, Old Rainlane Town
stepOne.worldNameTitle: What should this world be called for now?
stepThree.save: Save and enter the world handbook
stepTwo.adjustHint: Beginners should keep the defaults; only adjust when you clearly want a smaller or larger world.
stepTwo.preset.epic.desc: Best for many forces, locations, and multi-thread conflicts that need a stronger map and relationship structure.
stepTwo.preset.epic.title: Complex ensemble
stepTwo.preset.light.desc: Best for short pieces, a single main thread, and low complexity: get a clear, easy-to-write story stage first.
stepTwo.preset.light.title: Light stage
stepTwo.preset.standard.desc: Best for most full-length web novels; generates enough rules, forces, locations, and opening entry points by default.
stepTwo.preset.standard.title: Standard full-length
stepTwo.scaleHint: The scale determines how many rules, factions, concrete forces, key locations, and opening entry points AI generates. "Standard full-length" is recommended by default.
